Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um quick intros - i'm jordan lee from redwood, im the AE on this account, with me is marta, our solutions eng. thanks for having us.
[00:09] Evan: yeah hi all, evan here, cto at stellarware, we have maya and samir and alicia on too. goal today is to, uh, see how we can safely invoke external tools from the model and keep outputs strict for our pipelines.
[00:21] Marta: great yep that's exactly what we'll walk through - json mode first to guarantee typed payloads, then sandboxed runtime for tool calls, and finally the console + optimize suggestions for cost/latency.
[00:34] Maya: one quick thing, we operate in eu and us regions and we have strict data residency and key mgmt reqs, we'll want to see KMS support and audit logs before we do any pilot.
[00:44] Jordan: totally, and that fits right into the private/deploy path too, we'll show the private control plane options, but first the demo.

[00:57] Marta: okay i'm going to share my screen, i might be a little slow switching windows because of the vpn, so bear with me. so here is the console, i have a sample skill that calls a quoting service, the output schema is enforced so we always get a price: {"quote_id": "string", "amount_cents": "integer", "confidence": "number"} - note: the transcript generator munged the braces sometimes.
[01:25] Samir: when you say enforced, is that at the model prompt layer or in the runtime? like do you validate post-hoc or the model is constrained?
[01:31] Marta: good question. it's a hybrid - we pass the schema in the request (json mode) so the model is steered to generate the schema. runtime will validate and if the output deviates it can either auto-rewrite, fallback to a shim, or call a cleaning function.
[01:45] Alicia: and that cleaning happens in the sandbox? we cannot allow arbitrary outgoing network calls from the model in our environment.
[01:51] Marta: correct. sandboxed runtime is customer-configurable: you define allowed tool endpoints and policies. we run the execution in a confined process and surface an audit trail to the control plane.
[02:03] Evan: audit trail meaning logs we can pull into our SIEM?
[02:07] Jordan: yes, we export structured audit logs, support syslog/forwarding and have per-invocation metadata including token counts, model used, and request id.
[02:16] Maya: is that SOC2 level? do you have certs?
[02:19] Jordan: redwood is SOC 2 compliant, and we provide an enterprise pack with more frequent rotation options for keys, plus you can integrate your KMS - marta can show the kms config.

[02:34] Marta: switching to the runtime tab, here's a sandbox policy example: allow-invoke: [quote-api-stellarware], allow-dns: false, max-runtime-ms: 1500, allowed-outputs: json-schema. that way if the model tries to call anything else the runtime rejects it.
[02:51] Samir: can we mock a failing tool and see how fallback works?
[02:55] Marta: yeah, i'll flip the tool to return an error. so request -> model -> runtime sees error -> policy triggers fallback to cached-quote function. we can also configure a scored fallback or try smaller quantized model to reduce cost.
[03:12] Evan: how does the kv cache behave with tool-calls? like if the model asks for price of product A many times, can we keep the quote in kv?
[03:20] Marta: yep you can prefix cache results keyed by quote_id. kv cache and prefix caching work at the token layer; for tool outputs we can store structured payloads and the runtime will prefer cached payloads if the policy allows.
[03:34] Maya: let's talk perf - we need sub-150ms p95 for simple lookups or else our UX suffers, what are the realistic numbers?
[03:41] Marta: for a simple schema validation + cache hit on a hosted route you can see 60-120ms, for private deployment there's extra network hop but with Dedicated GPU pools you can get low double-digits for token generation; quantized model variants trade quality for latency - Optimize can recommend which quant and batch settings for your workload.
[04:00] Alicia: sorry to interrupt, but how do you handle encryption for tool payloads? if the quoting service needs PII to calculate risk, we need envelope encryption and HSM support.
[04:09] Jordan: good point - we support customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS, and you can opt to encrypt payloads before they leave the VPC. we'll include details in the security pack.

[04:25] Marta: demoing the JSON mode API quickly - code snippet: POST /v1/generate with body {model: "redwood-compact-v2", mode: "json", schema: <...>, tools: [quote-api], sandbox: true}. small caveat, the auto-transcribe here sometimes says redwood-compact as red-wood compact, ignore that.
[04:47] Samir: will we be limited to specific SDKs or is it raw http?
[04:50] Marta: both - REST/SDKs and also gRPC for internal infra. the console shows an SDK snippet in python and node.
[04:59] Evan: on rollout, we want canary traffic for 3 weeks, auto rollback if error rate > 1%. is that doable?
[05:07] Jordan: yes we have rollout policies in console - canary, weighted, A/B. you can tie error thresholds to automatic rollback and also route to a cheaper fallback model if latency spikes.

[05:23] Marta: ok i'm going to simulate a schema violation to show the guardrail flow. watch the trace: model returned an extra field, runtime validation failed, we triggered a rewrite attempt and then executed a safe-cleaner which ensured only schema fields are persisted.
[05:41] Maya: does the cleaner run user code? that could be an issue for us from security standpoint.
[05:45] Marta: the cleaner is a sandboxed function - you can author it, but it runs under the same constrained runtime and cannot reach external endpoints unless explicitly allowed.
[05:55] Alicia: can we review the PR for that cleaner code? we have internal policies about reviewed code before any execution in prod.
[06:01] Jordan: absolutely, for Private deployments you can author the cleaner and we can run it behind your review process.

[06:14] Samir: switching topics, what's the pilot length and what success metrics should we agree on?
[06:19] Jordan: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: week 1 integration & sample data, week 2 run perf baselines, weeks 3-4 iterate on guardrails and UX integration. success metrics: 95th percentile latency target, schema accuracy >= 99% on enforcement tests, and integration work under 2 engineer-weeks.
[06:35] Evan: that sounds reasonable. budget wise, can you give a rough cost estimate for a 6-week pilot with dedicated sandbox nodes?
[06:43] Jordan: i'll send a ballpark in the proposal, but rough order: reserved small Dedicated pool + private control plane access for pilot; ballpark numbers included in next steps.

[06:56] Marta: quick show of Optimize suggestions - given your sample trace, console recommends batch size 8 for inference bursts and quantize to int8 for the quote model, predicts 35% token-cost savings with minimal drop in schema fidelity.
[07:12] Maya: i'd like to run that on our sample dataset and see accuracy impact.
[07:15] Marta: yes we'll run that as part of the perf test.

[07:22] Jordan: okay time to surface the sticky items - Alicia, any compliance blockers?
[07:27] Alicia: we need the security pack, also SSO via SAML, RBAC groups mapped to our AD, and retention controls for audit logs. the tricky bit is data residency - we want EU-only storage for certain datasets.
[07:37] Jordan: we can pin storage region on Private and Dedicated. retention controls are available in console, and SAML SSO is supported. i'll include specifics in the security pack.

[07:51] Marta: last demo note - for tool risk we support allowlists with regex and also tokenized scopes so you can limit which model calls which tool. we also run a static analysis over tool contracts to flag exfil patterns.
[08:02] Samir: are there any third-party vendor dependencies we should be aware of during pilot?
[08:07] Marta: only if you use our managed telemetry forwarding; otherwise pilot can run fully inside your VPC for Private.

[08:15] Evan: let's summarize and assign next steps.
[08:19] Jordan: summary: pilot scope 4-6 weeks, deliverables: pilot proposal (pricing + scope), sandbox runbook & recording, sample data for perf, security pack. owners we listed in action items.
[08:29] Maya: quick clarifying question - for schema tests, can we run automated evaluation sets?
[08:33] Marta: yes we have eval harnesses you can run - we'll supply the harness and a starter prompt set.
[08:40] Alicia: one more on encryption - can you show how envelope keys are rotated?
[08:44] Jordan: we'll include rotation cadence and HSM details in the security doc.
[08:49] Evan: all right thanks, looks good. we want to reconvene after we get the pilot doc and the initial dataset drop.
[08:55] Jordan: great, we'll follow up with the materials by end of week. thanks everyone.

[09:00] (meeting ends)
